name: Bath
summary: Bath is a honey-coloured Georgian city built around hot springs the Romans turned into a temple and bathhouse. Its sweeping crescents, the abbey and a modern rooftop spa make it one of England's most beautiful cities, and Stonehenge is an easy trip away.
seasonNote: Spring to early autumn is best for walking. The Jane Austen Festival is in September and the Christmas market from late November. Summer weekends are busy with day-trippers.
arrival: Trains from London Paddington take about 1.5 hours. Bristol Airport is 45 minutes away by bus.
gettingAround: The centre is compact and walkable; buses run to the outskirts.
cashTip: Cards and tap payments work almost everywhere, even for small amounts; tipping about 10 to 12.5 percent in restaurants is common if service isn't included.
foodTip: Sally Lunn buns, cream teas with scones, and a Sunday roast in a pub.
buyTip: Bath soap and cosmetics, Jane Austen gifts, and local cider.

items.name: Roman Baths
items.summary: A Roman temple and bathing complex around a steaming natural hot spring.

items.tip: Visit late in the day when it's lit by torches in summer.
